newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower, second-tiers highlighted.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower, second-tiers highlighted.

text.p: Stocks closed Saturday's half-day session slightly lower on immediate profit-taking following steep gains in the past two days, brokers said.
The composite stock index shed 1.38 points to 781.49. Despite the index fall, advancers led gainers by 468 to 335 with 89 stocks going limit up.
"The market soared in the past two days without settling negative factors surrounding it. So investors tried to take quick profits today," said a Coryo Securities broker.
Gloomy economic outlook and unbalanced demand/supply of stocks took their toll on the market, brokers said.
But many second-tier shares continued to attract strong buying interest as the government will allow margin trading in the secondary shares from September.
Both Hansol Telecom and Seoul Foods went limit up, each gaining 3,000 won and 450 won to close at 53,000 and 8,000 respectively.
Hit by a series of negative economic statistics, many blue chip manufacturers slipped. Samsung Electronics shed 2,400 won to 61,400 and KEPCO fell 100 won to 24,900.
